question: Does the memetic hybrid (evolution + lifetime learning + inheritance of learned weights) beat its parts at an equal training budget?
data: sklearn bundled real datasets: breast_cancer, wine, digits; 20 random 60/20/20 splits each; test split used once
first_look_5_splits: hybrid looked +1.6 pp better than plain training — an artefact of too few splits
v1_20_splits: see neuro_experiment_v1_summary.txt: hybrid vs plain training 23/14/23, p=0.96; vs logistic regression 10/21/29, p=0.03
conclusion: NEGATIVE: on these datasets the hybrid adds nothing over plain training, inheritance of learned weights shows no significant effect, and plain logistic regression is significantly better. Pure neuro-evolution is far worse.
decision: neuro-memes stay as a meme TYPE under a simple-reference gate (must beat majority and a linear model on validation, else the linear model is adopted); neuro training is NOT deployed to the live node.
